newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber output down 1.6 pct in October.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber output down 1.6 pct in October.

text.p: Malaysia's rubber output fell 1.6 percent to 96,296 tonnes in October from a month earlier, but was 1.4 percent higher that the 94,991 tonnes produced in October 1995, the Statistics Department said.

Cumulative production for the first 10 months this year was 892,832 tonnes, down 0.9 percent from 901,210 tonnes recorded in the same period last year, the national Bernama news agency said, quoting the report.
Rubber stocks at the end of October totalled 194,512 tonnes, down 1.7 percent from end-September, but 18.6 percent higher compared with 164,045 tonnes at end-October 1995.

Exports in October rose 6.4 percent from September to 90,736 tonnes, while total exports for January-October 1996 fell 5.2 percent to 807,699 tonnes from 851,955 tonnes for the corresponding period last year, Bernama said.

Major importers of Malaysian rubber in the first 10 months this year were U.S. (98,625 tonnes), South Korea (80,660 tonnes), China (69,437 tonnes), Germany (61,329 tonnes), Britain (36,313 tonnes), Italy (35,636 tonnes) and Japan (34,888 tonnes). Together, they accounted for 51.6 percent of Malaysia's total exports during the period.

The department said Malaysia imported 21,113 tonnes of rubber in October, 11.3 percent lower than the preceding month, but 59 percent higher than the 13,281 tonnes imported in October 1995. Imports for the first 10 months this year totalled 222,127 tonnes, up 14.6 percent from 193,759 tonnes in the same period last year.
Domestic consumption in October was 31,842 tonnes, compared with 31,030 tonnes the previous month and 30,127 tonnes in October 1995.
